answer: Because the timing is recorded against the karst challenge, the plume audit can replay the anchor history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm hence has to pad 63 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A farm of 3718 identities would post 4591 proofs and burn roughly 4 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
